title: [Bug]:  error 'eglQueryDeviceAttributeXT: Bad attribute'
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

32.0.0 & 32.0.1

### Build Tool
electron-vite: 2.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Sonoma 14.6.1

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

31.4.0

### Expected Behavior


I don't want to encounter the error 'eglQueryDeviceAttributeXT: Bad attribute

### Actual Behavior

When I started the development environment (npm run dev), the console reported the following error, and it was continuously outputting this error:
```bash
[18489:0822/130231.159571:ERROR:gl_display.cc(497)] EGL Driver message (Error) eglQueryDeviceAttribEXT: Bad attribute.
[18489:0822/130231.525693:ERROR:gl_display.cc(497)] EGL Driver message (Error) eglQueryDeviceAttribEXT: Bad attribute.
[18489:0822/130231.758610:ERROR:gl_display.cc(497)] EGL Driver message (Error) eglQueryDeviceAttribEXT: Bad attribute.
[18489:0822/130232.026468:ERROR:gl_display.cc(497)] EGL Driver message (Error) eglQueryDeviceAttribEXT: Bad attribute.

[18489:0822/130232.966085:ERROR:gl_display.cc(497)] EGL Driver message (Error) eglQueryDeviceAttribEXT: Bad attribute.
```

**Context**:
Mac Mini Intel 2012
macOS 12.7.6 Monterey
node v20.17.0
electron v32.2.0

To avoid `EGL Driver message (Error) eglQueryDeviceAttribEXT: Bad attribute` in my electron project, main.js starts with:
```
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron')
if (process.platform === 'darwin' && process.arch === 'x64') {
	app.disableHardwareAcceleration()
}
```

comments.author: participant14
comments.body:
> It seems that this issue depends on the OS version and hardware. Some people use OpenCore to run newer macOS versions on old MacBooks, which appears to cause this problem.

While it _may_ be dependent on OS version and hardware (likely due to GPU hw specifically), it's not true to assume that only OpenCore running unsupported newer OS on older Apple hardware is the culprit.

Case in point:

[Reproduced on macOS Monterey `12.7.6`][1], which is the last official Apple-supported OS version for a MacBook Pro (`Retina, 13-inch, Early 2015`).  (This hardware has GPU: `Intel Iris Graphics 6100 1536 MB`)

**EDIT:** Just tested again with Chromium `133.0.6943.98`, same machine. Still happening on this version.

[1]: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/43415#issuecomment-2421635097
